definition: Tremulous means shaking slightly from emotion or nervousness.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word tremulous. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know tremulous should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: He signed the loan papers with a tremulous flourish, equal parts excitement and terror.
Wobbly stops short of tremulous — wobbly is a matter of balance, while tremulous is a fine visible shiver of feeling.
Convulsive goes further than tremulous — a convulsive shudder shakes the whole body, not just the voice or the hands.

Quivering names the physical motion — small, rapid trembling, whatever set it off: cold, wind, a plucked string. Tremulous keeps the same slight shake but adds the cause: feeling or nerves behind it. A leaf quivers in any breeze; a tremulous voice shakes because its owner is moved, thrilled, or afraid.

Shaky is the plain, all-purpose word for unsteady movement of any kind and any cause — a shaky ladder, shaky handwriting, a shaky start. Tremulous is finer and more human: a slight, visible shiver with emotion or nervousness behind it. Call the table shaky; save tremulous for the hand signing the papers.

Tremulous names a slight, visible shaking with feeling or nerves behind it—smaller than 'shaking,' more human than 'unsteady.' A voice, a hand, a smile can each be tremulous; an earthquake never is.
Tremulous is the writer's word for a small, telling shake — a voice, a signature, a candle-lit smile.
Plain 'shaky' does the everyday work.
Its unit-mate timorous is the temperament behind the shake: timorous is being easily frightened; tremulous is what the fright looks like.
